messages.message:
How the ISOCS baseline ("%err") uncertainty is correlated between energies. The baseline uncertainty is a systematic modeling/geometry uncertainty, so an efficiency that is (say) 5% high at one energy tends to be high at nearby energies too.

  • Fully correlated - the baseline uncertainty moves together across all energies (correlation ρ≈1). This is how GENIE treats these uncertainties, and is the default.
  • Gaussian (log-energy) - correlation falls off smoothly with the separation in ln(energy), controlled by the correlation length below.
  • Uncorrelated - each energy's baseline uncertainty is independent (ρ=0 between different energies).

The Monte-Carlo convergence ("%cnvrg") uncertainty is always treated as uncorrelated between energies.

The Gaussian correlation length, in natural-log-energy units, used when "Gaussian (log-energy)" correlation is selected. The correlation between two energies is ρ = exp(-½·((ln E₁ - ln E₂)/L)²).

For example, with L=0.35 two energies a factor of e (≈2.72) apart have correlation exp(-1/(2·0.35²))≈0.02, while energies 10% apart have correlation ≈0.96. Larger values make the uncertainty more correlated across energy.
